findings.title: Adding `order()` as an abstract SPI method breaks existing crypto providers
findings.body: `CryptoProvider` is an SPI loaded through `ServiceLoader`, so third-party implementations compiled against the previous interface will not implement this newly abstract method. They will either fail to compile when rebuilt or throw `AbstractMethodError` when `CryptoIntegration` invokes `order()` during provider detection. Make this a default method with a neutral priority (for example, `default int order() { return 0; }`) so existing providers remain usable while new providers can opt into prioritization.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion silently accepts signatures longer than the algorithm-defined size
findings.body: `concatenatedRSToASN1DER` copies only `signLength` bytes from the supplied raw JOSE signature and ignores any trailing bytes. Consequently, a valid ES256/384/512 signature with arbitrary bytes appended is converted to the same DER signature and can verify successfully, even though the JWS ECDSA signature has an invalid length. A too-short input also escapes as an unchecked `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`. Validate that `signature.length == signLength` before copying and reject mismatches with the method's declared `IOException`.

findings.title: ES384 and ES512 tests use a P-256 key rather than their required curves
findings.body: The test generates the default `EC` key pair, which is normally P-256, and reuses it for ES256, ES384, and ES512. As a result, the ES384/ES512 cases only test padding a P-256 scalar to a larger output size; they do not exercise P-384 or P-521 integer encodings, including the 67-byte signed `BigInteger` representation possible for P-521. Generate `secp256r1`, `secp384r1`, and `secp521r1` keys respectively and verify that the DER output after conversion is accepted by the corresponding public key.
